title: Deprescribing versus continuation of chronic proton pump inhibitor use in adults
authors: Boghossian TA, Rashid FJ, Thompson W, Welch V, Moayyedi P, Rojas-Fernandez C, et al.
population: 6 randomised trials in adult outpatients on daily PPI for at least 28 days with non-erosive reflux disease or Los Angeles grade A or B oesophagitis; 5 trials of on-demand use and 1 of abrupt discontinuation
funder: Internal sources: Bruyère Research Institute, Canada. External sources: Ministry of Health and Long-Term Care, Ontario, Health Services Research Fund, Canada; Ontario Pharmacy Research Collaboration (OPEN), Canada.
authorConflicts: Moayyedi received lecture fees, and his research chair is funded in part by an unrestricted grant from AstraZeneca to McMaster University; the Government of Ontario funded Farrell's institute to prepare a related deprescribing guideline.
result: On-demand use against continuous PPI use: lack of symptom control 157 against 92 per 1000 (RR 1.71, 95% CI 1.31 to 2.21; 5 trials, 1653 participants; low-quality evidence); pill use 3.79 fewer per week (4.73 to 2.84 fewer; moderate quality). Data were insufficient for conclusions on long-term benefits and harms of discontinuation.
